summary: Jackson County, AL 100-foot CCC steel tower built 1942 on Alabama Power land; likely removed before 1970; only four concrete footers reported to remain.

facts.status_note: Register says it was likely removed before 1970; the only remnants reported today are four concrete footers.
facts.agency: Alabama Power (landowner; 'Administered by' field). Tower was built for the Alabama Department of Conservation.

access.note: Tower stood on land owned by Alabama Power; no public access described in the sources read

events.note: Register 'Built 1942'; a July 1, 1942 Alabama Journal report announced the tower as completed
Register says 'before 1970' and 'likely removed before 1970'; exact removal date unknown

evidence.supports: standard 100-foot steel tower built by the CCC for the Alabama Department of Conservation on Alabama Power land
evidence.quote: This was a standard 100-foot steel tower built by the CCC for the Alabama Department of Conservation on land owned by Alabama Power.

evidence.supports: one of the last projects before the CCC shut down
evidence.quote: It was one of the last projects completed before the CCC shut down.

evidence.supports: only remnants today are four concrete footers
evidence.quote: The only remnants of the tower today are 4 concrete footers.

evidence.supports: tower at Russell's Point near Stevenson in Jackson County, completed by the state forestry division
evidence.quote: A new forest fire lookout tower, at Russell's Point near Stevenson in Jackson County, has been completed by the Alabama Conservation Department's division of forestry.
Forester Brooks Toler reported that four additional ones are under construction.
The new observation post is a 100-foot steel tower.

evidence.supports: CCC stopped building fire towers when the US entered WWII
evidence.quote: Upon America’s entry into WWII, the Civilian Conservation Corps ceased building firetowers

evidence.supports: Stevenson is in Jackson County, Alabama
evidence.quote: Stevenson is a city in Jackson County, Alabama

sources.title: Russell's Point (quoting the Alabama Journal, July 1, 1942)
Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Location conflict: the 1942 newspaper places the tower near Stevenson in Jackson County, but the register's latitude 33.8486 puts the pin about 110 km south of Stevenson (34.869 N). If the latitude is a typo for 34.8486, the point would sit about 8 km from Stevenson, which would fit the newspaper. That is plausible but unverified, so no correction is proposed; check on a topo map before changing the brief's coordinates. Agency: the brief's 'Alabama Power' is the register's administrator (landowner); the tower was built for the Alabama Department of Conservation, and both are kept. The 1970 removal year is an upper bound ('before 1970'). The 1942 newspaper's four additional towers were not traced further.
